description: standards/035-workers.md WK5 as data: what the platform's runner must do to start a one-shot worker, stated as seven verbs, each with the declaration fields (057 JB3) it consumes and the setting that satisfies it in each runner the standard names. The platform builds no runner; a renderer (WK6) targets this file and a checker reads it. A runner is admitted by satisfying every verb; a runtime whose runner cannot is not a runtime the platform deploys one-shots on.

verbs.requirement: Run an image, or a command in one, to completion with the declared arguments and environment, and expose the exit code to whatever invoked it.

satisfied_by.kubernetes: batch/v1 Job with restartPolicy: Never; status carries the container exit code
satisfied_by.systemd: Type=oneshot with ExecStart=; systemctl reports the result
satisfied_by.container_cli: docker run returns the exit code
satisfied_by.managed: ECS RunTask, Cloud Run Jobs, Nomad type=batch

verbs.requirement: Deliver SIGTERM and wait the declared grace before SIGKILL.
Kill a run that exceeds the declared deadline.
Fire a five-field cron expression evaluated in UTC, passing the scheduled instant to the one-shot as --at.

satisfied_by.systemd: OnCalendar=, translated from the cron expression
satisfied_by.container_cli: not a scheduler; the deployment and the operator are the other two triggers
satisfied_by.managed: EventBridge Scheduler, Cloud Scheduler, Nomad periodic.cron

verbs.requirement: Never start a second run of one schedule while one is running. The job locks anyway (057 JB6); this setting exists so the two never disagree.

satisfied_by.systemd: a timer never starts a unit that is already active

verbs.requirement: Never retry a failed run; the next tick is the retry, and 057 JB8 catches a job whose every tick fails.

satisfied_by.systemd: no Restart= on the oneshot unit

verbs.requirement: Handle a tick that could not fire on time by the declared policy: run once, late, within the window, or skip it.
